headline: Highest risk is open-webui’s broad network/MCP/file surfaces, but python-cheatsheet is documentation-only and non-interactive, so pairwise harms are mostly limited to prompt-injection and leakage via the web UI.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: open-webui can ingest files, browser content, and MCP/OpenAPI tool outputs, so attacker-controlled text could be treated as instructions. python-cheatsheet is documentation-only and non-interactive, so it is not itself an active injector, but it can still be copied into open-webui. The pathway exists in default web-UI workflows, though not via a direct agent-to-agent channel.
conditions: IF content from python-cheatsheet is pasted or imported into open-webui without provenance checks, THEN prompt injection is possible.
IF open-webui parses browser/file/MCP content as instructions, THEN attacker-controlled text can steer tool use.
mitigations: Disable automatic instruction-following from imported content.
Use a provenance banner for pasted/reference text.
Restrict open-webui tool access to a minimal allowlist.
Require manual review before executing tool outputs.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance tagging.

B_data_leakage.rationale: open-webui touches prompts, chat messages, documents, notes, calendar events, artifacts, persistent memory, files, and API keys, and it can call external APIs and mounted/local files. python-cheatsheet is read-only documentation, so it does not add a leak channel, but it can be used as a source document inside open-webui. The shared risk is leakage from open-webui’s broad data handling, not from the cheatsheet itself.
conditions: IF sensitive prompts, files, or API keys are loaded into open-webui, THEN they may be exposed through its external API calls or persisted memory.
IF the cheatsheet is copied into open-webui alongside sensitive context, THEN that context can be retained in chat artifacts.
mitigations: Avoid loading secrets into open-webui sessions.
Separate sensitive and non-sensitive workspaces.
Turn off persistent memory for sensitive tasks.
Review outbound connectors before use.
requires-engineering: enforce per-workspace data-loss controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: python-cheatsheet has no write, network, or execution capabilities, so it cannot contend for mutable resources. open-webui can write only through its own files/mounted volume and networked integrations, but there is no overlapping write surface with the cheatsheet profile. The pair therefore has only minimal conflict potential, mainly if the operator manually reuses the same workspace for unrelated content.
conditions: IF the operator manually places both agents on the same mutable directory, THEN open-webui may overwrite shared artifacts.
IF no shared writable resource exists, THEN capability conflict remains absent.
mitigations: Keep python-cheatsheet read-only.
Use separate directories for open-webui artifacts.
Avoid sharing git worktrees between the two.
Limit open-webui file-write permissions.
requires-engineering: add workspace locking for shared mounts.

D_cascading_error.rationale: open-webui can present retrieved or pasted content as chat context and can drive tool use, while python-cheatsheet is a reference source that may be treated as authoritative by a user or by open-webui-generated responses. There is no evidence of autonomous action in python-cheatsheet, but open-webui can propagate mistaken interpretations into downstream outputs unless the operator verifies them.
conditions: IF open-webui uses python-cheatsheet text as source material without verification, THEN errors can be amplified into generated answers.
IF downstream users act on open-webui outputs, THEN incorrect guidance can cascade into work products.
mitigations: Require citations for generated claims.
Cross-check outputs against the source page manually.
Disable autonomous tool execution for reference-only tasks.
Mark reference-derived answers as unverified.
requires-engineering: add source-grounding and verification gates.

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, residency, or certification mismatch is documented for python-cheatsheet, and open-webui’s profile does not specify a conflicting compliance regime. The only concrete compliance concern is that open-webui can handle API keys and persistent user data, so policy violations are possible if regulated data is entered. The other agent is not cited because it is documentation-only and does not process regulated data.
conditions: IF regulated data is entered into open-webui, THEN retention or residency policy violations may occur.
IF the cheatsheet remains documentation-only, THEN it does not itself create a compliance breach.
mitigations: Do not enter regulated data into open-webui.
Use a non-sensitive test account.
Review retention settings before use.
Keep API keys out of shared sessions.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls.
